Wr.description: Soils developed on Tertiary basalt bedrock and colluvium on undulating to rolling (3-32%) land. With poorly drained soils in depressions.

Wy.name: Wynyard Association
Wy.description: Soils developed on Quaternary sandy marine &/or estuarine deposits on level to gently undulating (<1-3%) plains.

YT.name: York Town Association
YT.description: Soils developed from Tertiary clays and gravels on gently undulating to gently rolling plains.

Yo.name: Yolla Association
Yo.description: Soils developed on Tertiary basalt bedrock and colluvium on rolling to steep (10-56%) land approximately 13km inland. Generally occurring above 300m altitude and between 1300mm and 1500mm rainfall.

Calcarosol.gloss: Soils that are calcareous (contain lime, often as soft or nodular carbonate) throughout or from close below the topsoil, without a clear increase in clay into the subsoil.

Chromosol.gloss: Soils with a clear or abrupt increase in clay from topsoil to subsoil (texture contrast), where the upper subsoil is neither strongly acid nor sodic.

Dermosol.gloss: Soils with a well-structured subsoil (it breaks into distinct peds) but no clear texture contrast, and not as iron-rich as a Ferrosol.

Ferrosol.gloss: Iron-rich soils without a clear texture contrast: typically deep, red or brown, friable, well-structured clays formed on basalt (the old 'krasnozems').

Hydrosol.gloss: Seasonally or permanently wet soils: most of the profile is saturated for at least two to three months in most years, often with grey or mottled subsoil.

Kandosol.gloss: Soils with a massive or only weakly structured subsoil of at least 15 % clay and no clear texture contrast (the old red, yellow and brown earths).

Kurosol.gloss: Soils with a clear or abrupt increase in clay from topsoil to subsoil (texture contrast), where the upper subsoil is strongly acid (pH below 5.5).

Organosol.gloss: Peat soils: made largely of organic matter, either a thick layer (more than 40 cm in the top 80 cm) or a shallower one resting directly on rock.

Podosol.gloss: Sandy soils with a subsoil layer where organic matter, aluminium and/or iron washed down from above have accumulated, often a bleached sand over a dark or rusty pan.

Rudosol.gloss: Barely formed soils: hardly any soil development beyond a minimal topsoil, so little more than the raw parent material, such as fresh sand, alluvium or stony rubble.

Sodosol.gloss: Soils with a clear or abrupt increase in clay from topsoil to subsoil (texture contrast), where the upper subsoil is sodic (exchangeable sodium 6 % or more) and not strongly acid; such subsoils typically disperse when wet, set hard when dry and drain poorly.

Tenosol.gloss: Weakly developed soils: a developed topsoil but little or no subsoil development, often sandy or gravelly.

Vertosol.gloss: Cracking clay soils (35 % clay or more) that shrink and swell, opening deep cracks when dry.
